scope: Independent visual-concept review of three new HAVENLINE UI boards, each showing landscape and portrait layouts plus visible minimap expansion

requirements.check: Three actual image boards are supplied and inspected; every board shows landscape and portrait plus a clearly related expanded-map presentation.
Each direction is materially distinct in composition, visual language or navigation treatment; differences go beyond accent-color swaps.
A clear primary movement/action hierarchy supports Havenline's simple automatic gameplay; no distracting proliferation of combat buttons or unexplained competing calls to action.
Essential status, navigation, minimap, legend and map-return affordances are legible at a plausible device viewing size; no garbled prominent labels.
HUD leaves broad, readable gameplay space and the player, immediate route, gates and camp interaction cues are not buried behind panels.
Visible UI stays within safe-looking margins without cutoffs, collisions, overlapping touch controls or edge-trapped close/back controls.
Portrait and landscape are coherent adaptations of the same direction with reflowed groups, readable scale and no squeezed landscape layout.
The shared stylized winter camp remains recognizable across all boards, including two gates/openings and a centered furnace; UI comparisons do not depend on replacing the game world.
Overall presentation is modern, creative, visually captivating and comfortable to look at through balanced contrast, disciplined color, clean spacing and restrained effects.

evidence_required: Actual original generated image for every board
Readable UI/details inspection at available source resolution

scoring.pass_requires: Every mandatory visual-concept check passes and every reviewed mandatory dimension scores strictly above 9.0

next_action: Wait for actual image paths, inspect them, record specific defects and repairs, then re-review corrected boards if necessary.
